column1: # tests/memfn/c10_onebyte.tsv -- C10's one-byte fixtures (R17-b' B2, r17b_prime.md
# rev 3 §3.1 row B2 [rev3 A8]). One row per one-byte CONSUMER KIND: a pattern whose
# compile holds a one-byte FIND site stating exactly that kind. Read by
# run_deleg_sites.sh check 5 from the MFROUTED records of a -DPCREC_CAND_TRACE
# build (PCREC_MF_ROUTE_TRACE=1). The rule, per fixture:
#   - the site (PF or MLINE) holds a record of the fixture's kind with a finder
#     row (a non-`-` row field: the kit routed it). WHICH row is the kit's
#     choice and is not pinned here (D157);
#   - no record of ANOTHER stated kind appears (K35: one witness per kind);
#   - an UNSTATED record (EDGE, VMSPAN, N7 ... state no kind) is no kind: the
#     rule skips it, by name, and it can neither satisfy nor spoil a fixture.
# The check also holds the file to a floor of DISTINCT kind values: all five of
# the kinds named below (a literal in the script, not a count of this file).
# PRE's composite states DFA_SCAN, HYB_PF, VM_ATTEMPT and DFA_ATTEMPT too but is
# unrouted (its records read `-`), so those four kinds have NO witness here
# until PRE routes (B3b); the PF/MLINE fixtures witness the same kind values at
# the FIND sites.
# The expectations come from the design (§1.6/§4.3), not from a recorded run.
# (D172 S3: `\B(?<!a)d`, a fixed-width cover since S3, became `\B(?<!a)d+`.)
